topic: Research: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service Build 2026: Hosted Agents, Memory, Toolboxes, Evaluations, and Governance

key_points: Official Build 2026 recap positions Microsoft Foundry as a production agent platform with runtime, tools, memory, grounding, models, observability, and governance.
Highlights hosted runtimes, Toolboxes, memory, Voice Live, Foundry IQ, new MAI models, managed compute, and trust/evaluation capabilities.
Useful for fact-checking launch status: Foundry IQ knowledge bases are generally available; several agent and security features remain preview or limited access.
Frames Agent Service as the bridge from prototype agents to production operations.
Emphasizes framework choice: Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Agent SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK, or custom code.
Key enterprise value proposition is managed hosting, identity, scaling, observability, optimization, and Microsoft 365 distribution.
Defines Foundry Agent Service as a managed platform for building, deploying, and scaling AI agents.
Explains the two core operating models: prompt agents managed entirely by Foundry and hosted agents where teams package their own code as containers.
Clarifies the Responses API as a single entry point and positions agents as multi-step systems that call tools, use external data, and act autonomously.
Independent developer news summary of the Build 2026 Foundry announcements.
Explains why runtime, tooling, memory, and governance matter more than another model endpoint for production agent systems.
Good competitor framing for readers comparing Microsoft Foundry to generic agent frameworks or cloud-hosting approaches.
Independent analysis that Microsoft is competing on enterprise agent infrastructure rather than model novelty alone.
Positions Foundry as a control plane for agents, tools, context, evaluation, and governance.
Useful angle: enterprises need a governed operating layer for agents before they can move beyond demos.

stats.fact: Gartner predicts 40% of enterprise applications will include task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025.

Microsoft says Foundry Agent Service supports prompt agents and hosted agents; hosted agents can use Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Agent SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK, or custom code.

Hosted agents run as containerized applications: teams push an image to Azure Container Registry, then Foundry provisions compute, assigns a dedicated Microsoft Entra ID, exposes an endpoint, and handles scaling, session persistence, observability, and lifecycle management.
Hosted agents are billed based on underlying container compute consumed per hour, according to Azure pricing details.
Memory in Foundry Agent Service is a managed long-term memory solution with extraction, consolidation, retrieval, item-level CRUD, store-level retention defaults, and direct remember/forget commands.
Microsoft's agent development lifecycle explicitly includes tracing, repeatable quality and safety evaluations, hosted-agent optimization, publishing, monitoring, and iteration.
Microsoft announced ASSERT, an open-source policy-driven evaluation framework, and Agent Control Specification, a portable runtime control standard, at Build 2026.
IBM's 2026 survey of 2,000 CIOs and CTOs found that 77% say current governance frameworks are inadequate and only 11% feel fully prepared for large-scale AI deployment.

A June 2026 Forrester report covered by ITPro says about 75% of enterprise leaders report adopting agentic AI, but many initiatives remain stuck in pilot mode due to orchestration, governance, and trust costs.

Microsoft documentation warns that when hosted agents interact with third-party models, servers, or agents, customers are responsible for understanding data retention, location, and compliance boundary implications.

angles: Foundry Agent Service is best explained as an agent control plane, not just another agent framework: Microsoft is trying to own the runtime, identity, tool, memory, evaluation, and governance layers around whichever framework developers already use.

Hosted agents are the biggest Build 2026 shift for engineering teams because they let existing containerized agent code run on a managed endpoint with Entra identity, scaling, observability, and lifecycle controls.

The practical architecture pattern is build in code, package as a container, attach tools through Toolboxes, persist user context through Memory, ground enterprise data through Foundry IQ, then evaluate and govern with traces, ASSERT, and Agent Control Specification.
The buyer problem is no longer 'can we make an agent demo?' but 'can we operate many agents without duplicated auth code, hidden tool calls, unmanaged memory, or unverifiable policy compliance?'

Microsoft's preview labels matter: writers should distinguish GA capabilities like Foundry IQ knowledge bases from preview features such as hosted agents, Memory, Routines, Toolboxes, ASSERT, and ACS.

A strong differentiated section would compare Toolboxes, Memory, Foundry IQ, and Routines because they solve different forms of context and action: tools, persistent user state, enterprise knowledge, and scheduled execution.

Governance is the SEO wedge: most posts summarize announcements, but developer readers need concrete checkpoints for permissions, data boundaries, memory corruption, third-party model risk, and trace-based regression testing.

Pricing angle: hosted agents move agent cost discussion beyond tokens into container compute, Code Interpreter sessions, data grounding, evaluation runs, observability storage, and operational overhead.
